citations.quote: However, early-stage CubeSat design and mission conceptualization remain challenging for students and first-time developers because of fragmented tools and steep learning curves.

This paper presents NanoSatPlay, an AI-enabled, browser-based platform that unifies CubeSat design, configuration, orbit visualization, and intelligent design guidance within a single interactive environment.
By lowering technical barriers and emphasizing visual and experiential learning, NanoSatPlay enables rapid prototyping, systems-level understanding, and effective STEM education.
NanoSatPlay is implemented as a platform-independent web application. The front end is built using React and Next.js, with Three.js enabling interactive 3D visualization $ ^{[10]} $ .

AI-driven analysis and recommendations are powered by a Genkitbased backend. The system integrates four core modules: a CubeSat Designer, an Orbit Simulator, AI Design Assistant and AI enabled learning/assessment. All modules share a common data model, allowing real-time propagation of design changes across visualization, simulation, and AI feedback layers.

The CubeSat Designer offers a component-driven 3D interface for satellite assembly. Users select a standard CubeSat form factor (e.g., 1U or 3U) and populate it using a predefined library of subsystems including solar panels, batteries, antennas, sensors, and onboard electronics $ ^{[5]} $ .

The system continuously updates mass and power budgets and verifies compliance with platform constraints. This immediate feedback supports rapid experimentation while reinforcing key engineering trade-offs $ ^{[6]} $ .

The AI Design Assistant evaluates mission objectives and system configurations to assess feasibility and identify subsystem-level issues. Feedback is structured across major subsystems, including power, communication, and payload.
The assistant also recommends design improvements and connects users to relevant learning resources, enabling just-in-time, contextual instruction.
Users define key orbital parameters such as altitude and inclination and observe their effects on satellite trajectories through an interactive 3D environment.

citations.quote: The platform is built for rapid prototyping. Figure 6 shows the iterative CubeSat design improvement with the help of AI Design Assistant reduces time, cost and improves efficiency in launching to space.

A student can conceptualize a mission, assemble a preliminary design, simulate its orbit, and get AI feedback in a single session. This ability to quickly iterate and test ideas is a powerful learning tool that encourages experimentation and reinforces concepts through trial and error.

While the NanoSatPlay Orbit Simulator uses optimized trigonometric calculations for a fluid, real-time 3D visualization suitable for web browsers, its conceptual foundation is rooted in the core principles of astrodynamics.

NanoSatPlay demonstrates how AI-enabled web platforms can streamline nanosatellite education by unifying design, simulation, and intelligent assistance. The platform enables rapid conceptualization while promoting practical understanding of space systems engineering. Future work will expand subsystem fidelity and mission-level analysis capabilities.
